thread:
maria: Heads up — during last night's GPU backfill we saw ~1-4% packet drops between pods on the same node when heavy model shard syncs ran. Symptoms: increased gRPC retries and slow KV fetches, not full blackhole.

devon: Seen something similar on canary. Drops cluster-internal, east-west only, primarily when multiple pods saturate NIC TX. Any recent kernel/firmware rollouts? :thinking_face:

maria: No mass firmware pushes. Kernel was bumped on a subset to 6.1.14 last week for backport fixes. Only nodes in us-west2-acct1 were affected.

sasha: I grabbed a pcap during one run. Lots of small retransmits and bursts of reordered UDP (VXLAN). Capture snippet: `tcpdump -tnn -i vxlan0 udp and host 10.40.12.5` shows lots of duplicate ACKs.

jules: Could be offload interaction (GSO/GRO/LRO) with encapsulation. When VXLAN+GSO combine, kernel sometimes emits odd sized frames and NIC or switch drops them.

maria: Ran quick checks: `ip -s link show vxlan0` looks normal. `ethtool -k ens5` shows gso/gro on. I toggled `gro off` on a test node and the drop rate dropped to ~0.2% during same workload.

anil: Interesting. So turning GRO off reduced drops — that points to host-side reassembly issues. What's the CPU/softirq pressure? `cat /proc/softirqs` during the run?

maria: Softirq spikes aligned with the drop window. Also saw tx_queue_overflow increments on `cat /proc/net/softnet_stat`. Host level queuing looked stressed.

zoe: Any qdisc shaping on those nodes? We use `fq_codel` by default but had some `tc` experiments earlier this month.

devon: I checked — one kubelet change added `txqueuelen` tweaking on eni devices for high-throughput pods. Maybe combined with `fq_codel` it's worsening tail drops under bursts. `tc -s qdisc show dev ens5` shows lots of drops in backlog.

sasha: Also noticed RDMA nodes were unaffected — they use native IPoIB path for some services. So overlay-induced fragmentation seems likely culprit.

jules: Hypothesis: bursty east-west encapsulated traffic + GSO/GRO leads to oversized skbs that the NIC/switch can't handle post-encap, producing late drops. Packet reordering arises when multiple cores handle different fragments.

maria: Short mitigation I deployed: disabled GRO on vxlan interfaces on canary nodes and bumped txqueuelen from 1000 -> 3000 for GPU-heavy instances. Next backfill run had negligible retries. :thumbsup:

anil: Long term we should: 1) test kernel versions for regression, 2) coordinate NIC firmware upgrade with vendor, 3) consider offload policy: enable hardware tunnel offload if NIC supports VXLAN/Geneve; that should keep encap handling on NIC.

zoe: Also let's add a monitoring alert for `netdev_drops` and `softnet` backlog spikes tied to job tags so we get early signal before customer impact.

devon: Quick experiment script for canary: ```bash
# example probe
for n in 1 2 3; do
  kubectl -n infra exec -it probe-pod -- bash -c "ping -c 200 $TARGET && ip -s link show vxlan0"
done
```

sasha: I forwarded the pcap and kernel logs to NIC vendor. They requested ethtool stats during a reproduce. Also asked about `tx_hash` distribution across queues — could be hot-queueing under 5-tuple skew.

maria: Action items agreed: 1) infra team to run controlled reproducer on canary nodes with GRO toggles and collect ethtool stats (assigned to devon), 2) infra to open vendor support ticket with logs/pcaps (sasha), 3) add monitoring alert for netdev drops and softnet backlog (zoe), 4) hold kernel rollouts in us-west2 until we validate (maria).

jules: Addendum: If hardware tunnel offload isn't available, we may have to default to `gro off` for encap hot paths or tune `txqueuelen` + `fq_codel` params per instance type. Need perf tradeoffs.

maria: Thanks all — I'll post the test results in this thread. If anyone wants to help run repros this afternoon ping me. :coffee: 

infra-bot: deploy started: canary-probe-v2 in us-west2 (maria)
